text: Udupi district, also known as Udipi (IPA: [uɖupi]) in Kannada or Odipu (IPA: [oɖipu]) in Tulu, is an administrative subdivision in the state of Karnataka, India, with its headquarters in the city of Udupi. It lies in the Canara old north Malabar coastal region and comprises seven taluks, 233 villages, and 21 towns. The three northern tehsils—Udupi, Kundapur, and Karkala—were transferred from Dakshina Kannada district (South Canara) to form Udupi district on 25 August 1997. Moodabidri was officially established as a new tehsil in 2018. In February 2018, the district was further divided into three additional taluks, with Byndoor carved out of Kundapur taluk and Udupi taluk split into three parts: Kapu, Brahmavar, and Hebri, in addition to the original Udupi taluk. Dinakar Babu and Sheela K Shetty of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) are the current president (Sarpanch) and vice-president of the Udupi Zilla Panchayat, respectively, following the election held on 27 April 2016. The district is bordered by Uttara Kannada to the north, Dakshina Kannada to the south, Shimoga to the northeast, and Chikmagalur to the east, with the Arabian Sea to the west. It is connected by road and railway; National Highway 66 (formerly NH-17) is the main road, while National Highway 169A links it to Thirthahalli in Shivamogga, passing through Agumbe Ghat, which is narrow and allows only mini buses and mini lorries. National Highway 169 (formerly NH-13) from Mangaluru to Shivamogga passes through Sanoor, Karkala, Bajagoli, and Mudar. State highways (SH) and Main District Roads (M.D.R) are maintained by the Karnataka Public Works Department (P.W.D.). The Konkan Railway connects Udupi to Goa, Maharashtra, and Kerala, with railway stations at Udupi, Byndoor, Kundapura, Barkur, Innanje, and Padubidre; trains run to Bangalore, Mangalore, Kasaragod, Margao, Thane, and Mumbai. According to the 2011 census, Udupi has a population of 1,177,361, ranking 403rd out of 640 districts in India, with a population density of 304 inhabitants per square kilometre (790/sq mi), and a growth rate of 5.9% between 2001 and 2011. The district has 253,078 households, with 562,131 males and 615,230 females; children aged 0–6 number 103,160 (8.76% of the total), and the sex ratio is 1094 (1093 females per 1000 males), higher than Karnataka’s average of 973. The literacy rate is 78.69%, with 82.85% of males and 74.89% of females literate; 28.37% of the population lives in urban areas. Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes constitute 6.41% and 4.49% of the population, respectively. At the 2011 census, 42.70% spoke Kannada, 31.44% Tulu, 12.16% Konkani, 4.61% Urdu, 2.83% Marathi, 2.13% Malayalam, and 2.01% Beary as their first language. Udupi has a tropical monsoon climate with hot, humid summers (March to May, temperatures 30–34 °C) and heavy monsoon rainfall (June to September), with mild, dry conditions in December–February and occasional rainfall in October–November. It is one of Karnataka’s wettest districts, with long-term average annual rainfall between 4,200–4,500 mm (recent state summaries report ~4,535 mm), and exceptional totals in the mid-2010s, including over 5,900 mm in 2016. In June 2025, Udupi recorded 1,140 mm of rainfall, making it the highest-rainfall district in India for that month according to IMD/press summaries. In September 2020, the district received 315.3 mm of rainfall, a record in Udupi taluk over the last 40 years. A thermal power plant with 1200 MW installed capacity and a proposed 1600 MW expansion is located at Nandikoor. Suzlon operates a wind blade manufacturing facility at Padubidre, which faced a lock-out in November 2017 lasting over a month and was suspended again in July 2018. A strategic petroleum reserve is located underground in Padur (Padoor). At Shivalli Industrial Estate in Manipal, small-scale industries have established factories, including clay roof tiles (Mangalore tiles), cashew nut processing, coconut oil mills, and fish meal units. Many small entrepreneurs produce pickles, Happala (Pappad), spice powders, and other food products. Prior to the nationalisation of commercial banks and insurance companies in the early 1960s, the district had several private banks and insurance companies, including Syndicate Bank, Corporation Bank, and Canara Bank, which originated in this region (then South Kanara district) before India’s independence in 1947.
